clue.text: A way to intimidate one lacking in courage

parts.note: to cow someone is to frighten them into submission
taken as written
RD is the address abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A method of bullying someone who is short on bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: A coward is a person who lacks bravery, so this is a plain synonym phrase.

clue.text: Rider bound to get caught in the rain

indicators.note: the leap is trapped inside the downpour, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a shower is a brief fall of rain
to bound is to leap or jump

explanation.surface: A horseman is sure to be drenched by a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain to', but it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A showjumper is the equestrian who rides horses over fences in competition.

clue.text: Seasonal items of tableware

parts.note: suggests Christmas crockery, but here means used for seasoning food
the pots that hold salt, pepper, oil and vinegar on a stand

explanation.walkthrough: 'Seasonal' reads as festive; the pun is on seasoning food with salt and pepper.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruet set is a stand of condiment containers used to season food at the dining table.

clue.text: Small amount charged to top up medicine

indicators.note: in this clue the word top is turned upwards, read from its end back to its start

parts.note: taken as written
an ion is a tiny electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: A little extra paid to replenish one's supply of medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small amount charged' sounds like a fee, but it is an electrically charged particle.
explanation.definitionFit: A potion is a liquid dose of medicine, or in stories a magical drink.

clue.text: Found in Central American country, or in landscape generally

indicators.note: the word or is found within the country's name, so it sits inside it

parts.note: Panama lies between Costa Rica and Colombia
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something seen in Panama, or anywhere in the countryside at large.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, unbroken view of a whole landscape or region.

clue.text: Inflicted pain on foreign tutor of socialist persuasion

indicators.note: something foreign is strange or altered, so the letters of tutor are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
red is the colour of left-wing politics

explanation.surface: An overseas teacher with left-wing views was made to suffer.
explanation.definitionFit: To torture someone is to deliberately cause them severe suffering, so this is a synonym.

clue.text: Husband number three is ready to have a ball!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a woman's third husband is her ...

definitions.text: is ready to have a ball
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the cricket fielder waiting behind the slips for the ball

explanation.walkthrough: Third man is a cricket fielding position behind the wicket on the off side; the clue makes it sound like a party invitation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works both as a third husband and as a cricket fielder positioned to receive the ball.

clue.text: Grow sad when vehicle stops short

indicators.note: cut short means losing the final letter of the word

parts.note: a moped is a small motorbike

explanation.surface: Someone gets gloomy when their car breaks down unexpectedly.
explanation.definitionFit: To mope is to be listless and dejected, so this is a loose synonym.

clue.text: Tidier without Lawrence in the vicinity

indicators.note: without means lacking, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: neater is a comparative synonym
T. E. Lawrence, 'Lawrence of Arabia', is known by his initials

explanation.surface: Things are tidier nearby once Lawrence has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Near means close by, which is a synonym of in the vicinity.

clue.text: Two chaps meet as usual

parts.note: the first of two chaps: Norm, a man's name
the second chap: Al, another man's name

explanation.surface: A pair of men get together as they always do.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal means conforming to the standard or ordinary state, a synonym of usual.

clue.text: Attractive shade of green for a plant

parts.note: sweet means charming or pleasing
pea green is a light yellowish green

explanation.surface: A pretty green colour chosen for a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a climbing flower grown for its scented blooms.

clue.text: They're a revolutionary form of entertainment

definitions.text: They're a revolutionary form of entertainment

parts.note: suggests political upheaval, but means going round in circles
fairground rides

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests a radical new show; it means literally spinning round.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundabouts are merry-go-rounds, fairground rides that rotate.

clue.text: Family man or a philanthropist

parts.note: blood means kinship, as in blood relatives
Don is a man's name, and a don is a university fellow
taken as written

explanation.surface: Choosing between being a family man and a generous benefactor.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood donor gives blood freely to help strangers, a playful kind of charitable giver.

clue.text: Planet almost entirely consumed by flood

indicators.note: all but the last letter of the planet's name is kept

parts.note: Saturn is the ringed sixth planet
ate means eaten up

explanation.surface: A world nearly swallowed up by a great deluge.
explanation.definitionFit: To saturate is to soak something completely, so it is a verb synonym of inundating.

clue.text: Support leader against the others

parts.note: a head is the person in charge
the rest means the remaining ones

explanation.surface: Back the boss in opposition to everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' looks like a verb meaning to back someone; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A headrest is a cushioned prop for the back of the head, as on a car seat.

clue.text: Expert has nothing on master criminal

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it
criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters of master are twisted

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A specialist knows nothing about a criminal mastermind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master criminal' reads as one phrase, but master is the fodder and criminal its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished expert, especially a musician or conductor.

clue.text: Cut out pointless utterance

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
without a point, meaning one compass point letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Compass points N, S, E and W are crossword 'points'; here one E goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To truncate is to shorten something by chopping off part of it.

clue.text: Man without headgear is the object of one's animosity

indicators.note: in its old sense, without means outside, so the man surrounds the hat

parts.note: Pete is a man's name
a hat is worn on the head

explanation.surface: A bareheaded man is the one you dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking, but here it means around the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet hate is a particular thing someone strongly dislikes, a target of special annoyance.

clue.text: Experimental form of transport

definitions.meaning: first meaning: avant-garde, outside the mainstream
second meaning: a subway or metro railway

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a trial vehicle; the two halves are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes radical alternative art and also names an urban railway running below the streets.

clue.text: Disturbing business?

parts.note: a loud, unsettling din
a dishonest scheme for making money

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that two senses are blended: noise that disturbs and a crooked trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is both an uproar and a fraudulent money-making operation.

clue.text: Film music playing as I left

indicators.note: the remaining letters are played about with and rearranged
I has left, so that letter departs

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A movie soundtrack is playing as I walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie; it is a layer on a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum is a thin layer of dirt or froth on a liquid's surface.

clue.text: Heard to come down heavily on the less well-off

indicators.note: heard means listened to, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: to pour is to rain hard

explanation.surface: Rumoured to be cracking down hard on people with less money.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor means having little money, an adjective synonym of financially worse off.

clue.text: Quick to make a cutting remark

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an exclamation urging speed
second meaning: playfully, the sound of chopping twice

explanation.walkthrough: A cutting remark is usually sarcasm; here it is literally the noise of chopping.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a colloquial call to hurry up, and literally sounds like repeated cuts.

clue.text: Predicament arising from drunken capers

indicators.note: drunken suggests staggering about, so the letters of capers are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tight spot that came out of tipsy antics.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward situation, an informal synonym of a jam or fix.

clue.text: A long-running event

parts.note: sounds like a show with a long run, but means involving a long run
a race over about 26 miles

explanation.walkthrough: 'Long-running' suggests a show with a long run; taken literally it is a long race on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a footrace of just over 26 miles.

clue.text: Failing to leave the country

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flaw or shortcoming (noun)
second meaning: to abandon one's nation for another, as a spy might

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an excuse for not emigrating, but the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A defect is a fault, and to defect is to desert one's homeland for a rival state.
